Retrieved memory from a prior similar clinical case. Historical note: similar symptom clusters may suggest a specific diagnosis.
You must output exactly the following diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception

speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand your condition better, are you having any episodes of severe, colicky abdominal pain or vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound. Are the episodes of pain intermittent, with the baby drawing their knees up or passing stool containing blood and mucus?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound not performed; however, clinical history indicates episodes of pain are not described as intermittent with the baby drawing knees up, and stool containing blood and mucus was not reported.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the update. Since the classic intermittent, colicky pain and "currant jelly" stools are not present, could you tell me if there are any specific signs like a sausage-shaped mass in your abdomen, or if the vomiting has become green or bilious? Also, does the baby have any fever or appear lethargic?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Physical_Examination_for_mass.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Physical Examination for Mass: A sausage-shaped mass is not palpable upon examination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the classic signs of intussusception (intermittent pain, currant jelly stools, and a sausage-shaped mass) are absent, and we have not yet performed an X-ray or blood work, do you know if the baby has passed any stool recently, and has the vomiting become green?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-ray: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction; Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Normal.
